findings.detail: The question has the same problem as M2-S29-T1. Both give one predictable, same-steps-every-time workflow and one open-ended investigation whose findings change the next step. Both ask the reader to match the first to a fixed prompt chain and the second to dynamic decomposition, so the same reasoning leads to the answer. Splitting one dispute into two phases only changes the setting, not the choice. Option D also repeats the wrong option of M1-S21-T1 almost word for word: plan every subtask from the first message, then run that plan without revising it after tool results arrive.

blind_answer.reason: The investigation phase is open-ended and its findings change the next step, so it needs dynamic decomposition (A). The pre-refund phase checks the same four points for every case, so a fixed prompt chain with one focused pass per point fits it (C). B risks diluting attention across the four checks. D ignores what the tool results reveal. E lets the agent skip checks that must run every time.
